stances.claim: Judicial rule-making is the better path to enforcing economic rights -- superior to congressional action -- because it is constitutionally faultless, derived from the SC's explicit power under Art. VIII Sec. 5 par. 5.

stances.claim: The economic rights already enshrined in the Constitution are sufficient raw material for PALS to identify which can be enforced via judicial writs -- no new legislation needed.

The entrepreneurship category presents the most politically consequential challenge: the government reneges on agreements, delays decisions, and treats entrepreneurs unfairly -- a writ must be able to compel government to honor its commitments.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban continues his previous Sunday's writ-of-prosperity proposal, reporting that Dean Joan Largo of the University of San Carlos -- newly installed as PALS president -- 'happily agreed' to make the writ the centerpiece of her two-year incumbency. He argues that judicial rule-making is the better path to enforcing economic rights: superior to congressional action because it is constitutionally faultless, derived from the SC's explicit power under Art. VIII Sec. 5 par. 5 -- citing prior SC exercises including the Rules of Court, the 2010 Rules of Procedure for Environmental Cases, and the August 2018 Rule on Precautionary Departure Order. Using the three general ways of earning a living as the organizing framework, CJ identifies: (1) employment -- crafting a writ compelling government to provide adequate employment, assure living wages, and protect workers, with OFWs adding cross-border complexity; (2) self-employed professionals -- doctors, lawyers, farmers, fisherfolk; and (3) entrepreneurship -- where the Constitution recognizes the private sector as the engine of growth, yet the government frequently reneges on agreements and delays decisions. How to craft a doable writ of prosperity for all three categories and ensure wellbeing for all under the rule of law is described as PALS's major task, to begin with Dean Largo's October 12 keynote lecture.
